abstract:
BackgroundEndurance exercise reduces cardiovascular disease risk, but how this protection is mediated at the molecular level remains incompletely understood.

MethodsUsing multi-omic data from MoTrPAC, we integrated 13,790 selected molecular features across eight cardiac omic layers from 50 female and male rats undergoing 1-8 weeks of endurance training, as well as sedentary controls. Multi-omic temporal programs were defined using MOFA/MEFISTO and compared to physiological adaptation, human cardiac disease signatures, causal cardiomyopathy genes, and cross-tissue responses.

ResultsSeven temporal programs of coordinated molecular responses were identified across cardiac omic layers. Transient metabolic responses showed sex-dependent timing and generally preceded sustained structural changes with limited correspondence to skeletal muscle, while complement proteins declined with training. Among these, a sustained program was associated with improvement of VO2max and accounted for 38 of 50 significant overlaps with human cardiac disease signatures, frequently with opposing molecular responses, including reduced Fn1 and increased Klhl40 transcript and protein abundance by 8 weeks. To provide mechanistic context, we examined 112 genes causally linked to inherited cardiac disease, finding significant training-associated changes in 72 genes at the transcript level and 57 at the protein level. Notably, FLNC, BAG3, and PKP2 protein abundance increased, contrasting with reduced-dosage mechanisms in their respective cardiomyopathies. Conversely, disease-aligned and disease-opposing chaperone responses suggested coordinated protein quality-control mechanisms that may contribute to exercise-mediated cardioprotection.

ConclusionsEndurance training induces coordinated, time-dependent molecular responses across cardiac pathways implicated in human disease, including both disease-opposing changes in known causal genes and disease-concordant stress responses.

C_LIO_LIFemale and male hearts engaged broadly shared metabolic pathways with sex-specific timing of mitochondrial protein and post-translational responses.
C_LIO_LISustained programs account for most overlaps with human cardiac disease signatures, frequently with opposing molecular responses; increased FLNC and BAG3 further suggest potential compensation for reduced-product cardiomyopathy mechanisms.

What are the clinical implications?O_LIEndurance training induces molecular responses that significantly overlap with cardiovascular disease signatures. Both disease-opposing and disease-aligned regulation may help distinguish potentially protective adaptations from pathological remodeling.
C_LIO_LITraining upregulates several causal cardiomyopathy genes implicated in haploinsufficiency, suggesting potential compensation for reduced gene dosage across distinct genetic disease contexts.
C_LIO_LIFemale and male hearts have distinct temporal responses in excitation-contraction coupling, metabolism, and cytoprotection, highlighting potential sex-specific mechanisms of cardiac adaptation.
